title: Merkalis: Conquest - Battle spells demo
author: Fickle_Excuse_6680
selftext:
Hey!!! Here is my **Merkalis: Conquest** gnd real-time strategy game battle spells demo... 

How i use AI:

 Claude code - for coding, ChatGPT - for pictures, MeshyAI - for 3d modeling.

I'd love to hear your thoughts and feedback!

Also, a quick reminder that the **free demo** is already available on Steam. Thanks for checking it out!  
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5268040/Merkalis\_Conquest/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5268040/Merkalis_Conquest/)

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
Oooh, conceptually I love this. Like a very lite version of Total Warhammer.

Are there plans for a big campaign map, or is that out of scope? 

  
I'll give it a play in a minute... from the trailer, my primary nitpitck would be that the combat seems to lack impact. How many iterations has this gone through so far? Have you already tried turn-based combat? 

Like, the cavlary feels like it should really hammer the infantry if it can connect with them, and shove them around. Also not a huge fan of the blobbing shown in the trailer; since the fidelity is lighter, surely we can get away with blobbing and do something more interesting?

replies.author: Fickle_Excuse_6680
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback! I'm working on maps and a campaign right now — there will be large maps, and the campaign will have a proper story with events.
As for combat, I did have an idea to make units weaker when hit from the flanks or the rear, but with the current format it turned out to be really awkward to implement, so I had to drop it. Turn-based isn't planned — I want the game to stay dynamic :)

replies.author: Fickle_Excuse_6680
replies.body: Regarding combat, I've already made fixes — the AI now has three difficulty levels, and I've added spells that you can find on the map, which change the picture dramatically. The video in the post is showing exactly those new spells, by the way.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
Okay; I played the demo.

  
I do feel like these is a solid foundation here, but IMHO the direction feels... muddy at the moment. I'll split my criticism into 3 layers:

Introduction and worldbuilding: Honestly, while the set-up is basic, I can get on board with this. 4 factions, good emperor died mYsTeRiOuSlY, gee whiz how unfortunate, i wonder what happened - now there is WAR!   
  
i'm in   
  
for your introduction, though - even though this is not too long-winded - I think you need to be even more efficient with the storytelling. Here is the introduction to HBS's Battletech game:   
  
[BATTLETECH - Intro Cinematic](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PAGY4UMScyU)  
  
No monologue needed; an incredibly complex history full of factions and political intrigue and a canon that fans are downright religious over compressed so skillfully into just 2 minutes of mostly still images. It's amazing.  
  
I think you could very easily set something like that as the north star for your introductory sequence - just reeling in the player so they want to know more.  
  
I would also... maybe workshop the names a bit. Good fantasy names are very hard, these aren't the worst names ever, just they just don't quite, for me, have the sauce they ought to have.  
  
  
Strategic Map:   
  
I really like how fundamentally simple this is... and I am also left asking, what is the point of it being 3D? Why not use 2D terrain and icons, like you do with the tactical map? Less resource intensive and it will look a lot better.

I would think about leaning even further into the automation of the system. Click-click-clicking everywhere to create more territory feels more clunky than engaging, IMHO... and I just don't see a reason the outposts can't just automatically expand the territory within their own borders. That way the player can just focus on setting up infrastructure.  
  
It's too clunky to have a modal window open when the player clicks an area with multiple things in it, then choosing a thing from that menu. No. Find a way to get it to be more responsive than that, so the player can just click a thing to select it.  
  
Tactical Map:   
  
...This is rough. It feels incredibly bad to play, to the point where I wonder what the point is? You have a perfectly serviceable strategic layer with a lot of design space in it, and the autobattles felt pretty good. It doesn't feel like the tactical layer adds anything meanigful - it's just a more plodding rock paper scissors game that the AI is bad at playing and probably will never be good at playing.  
  
If it were me, I'd completely strip out the tactical layer, focus on tightening up the strategic layer and making that as fun as it can be, and incorporate spells / archery / etc into that layer somehow instead of trying to add a tactical layer for those effects.  
  
  
It's nice work so far.
